conviction_note: The sector got worse through Q3 and into October: mortgage rates went from 6.66% to 6.95% to 7.40%, the NAHB index fell 35 -> 32 -> 29, and both peers that reported since MHO last spoke (LEN, KBH) traded down on cautious margin and delivery outlooks. Against that, MHO's Q3 order comparison is easy (1,908 contracts, -6% a year ago), the stock is 20% off its August level and sits at about 0.96x June book with a fresh $250M buyback, and the skew already pays for downside. The findings net to -0.9; the scaled number is a slight negative lean (p_up 46 on a 4.5% absolute move) because the bad news is largely sector news the price already reflects.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $3.25 on revenue $1.11B (MarketBeat, 2026-10-14: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-mi-homes-mho-set-to-post-earnings-on-wednesday-2026-10-14/ ; TipRanks also lists $3.25). Benzinga disagrees at $3.35 EPS / $1.08B revenue (https://it.benzinga.com/quote/MHO/earnings-forecasts). EPS is on two agreeing sources; the revenue bar is disputed ($1.08B vs $1.11B), so the revenue-dependent finding is capped small. The company gives no quarterly guidance; its only stated target is average 2026 community count about +5%. Comparisons: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS $3.14 (GAAP $3.02), Q3 2025 EPS $3.92 on $1.132B revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest: Equibles shows 1.15M shares short at the 2026-03-13 settlement with 4.14 days to cover (range about 4-6.6 days over late 2025 and early 2026; https://equibles.com/stocks/mho/shortinterest). MarketBeat shows an undated 3.28% of float and 2.9 days. No September 2026 figure was found. This is not a crowded short. The baseline 25-delta skew is +4.27 vol points (downside paid), but the chain is near-unusable: ATM spread is 81% of mid, total OI 126, put/call OI 0.1, ATM IV 49.2% against 21.9% 20-day realised. Tape: -13.68% over 20 days, -24.45% from the 52-week high, 4.64% above the 52-week low, spot $123.15 against June 30 book value of $127.88 a share.

findings.finding: Rates and builder sentiment worsened through MHO's Q3 (Jul-Sep) and into October. Freddie Mac's 30-year rate was 6.66% at end-August, 6.95% in late September and 7.40% in early October. The NAHB index went 35 (Aug) -> 32 (Sep) -> 29 (Oct, the lowest since June 2012), and the share of builders cutting prices went 35% -> 38% -> 43%. MHO's call commentary on October traffic and on buydown costs will reflect this.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: MHO gives no numeric guidance, so its outlook is call commentary. On the Q3 2025 print, with orders down 6%, the stock fell 6.14%. On the Q2 2026 print, management cited choppy demand and rising rates and the stock still rose 1.54%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. MHO is -13.7% over 20 days and about -20% from roughly $154 in mid-August, ITB fell 7.3% in September, and the skew pays for downside. What is not yet priced is how MHO's own October sales pace and incentive load read against the 7.4% rate, which only the call reveals. If the market had fully priced a bleak October, the stock would trade well below book; at about 0.96x it is only marginally below.
findings.independence: This is a proxy and is macro-to-company. The September NAHB detail is at https://eyeonhousing.org/2026/09/builder-sentiment-falls-on-higher-interest-rates-and-costs/ and the August/September rate path at https://gvwire.com/2026/09/24/us-new-home-sales-jump-to-eight-month-high-in-august/. Counterpoint from the same release: August new home sales jumped to 684k SAAR, a 2026 high.

findings.finding: Both peers that reported after MHO's July 29 call guided cautiously and traded down. Lennar (Jun-Aug quarter, reported 2026-09-16): orders -9% to 20,879, below its own range; full-year deliveries cut to 80-81k from 82-83k; shares down about 4.6%. KB Home (2026-09-22): orders -12%, pace 3.1 vs 3.8 per community, Q4 housing gross margin guided 16-16.6% against 17.2% consensus; shares fell about 2% after hours despite an EPS beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer prints show beats being sold on margin outlook this cycle (KBH beat, fell; LEN missed, fell). MHO's own mixed prints: -6.14% (Q3 2025, orders down), +1.54% (Q2 2026, orders +15%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the sector sold off after these prints. What may not be priced is whether MHO's outperformance continues. Its Q2 orders were +15% while these peers' were negative. If the market expected MHO's orders to fall like the peers', consensus EPS would sit below Q2 adjusted $3.14 rather than above it at $3.25.
findings.independence: KBH release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000795266/000079526626000068/exh991kbh-earningsrelease0.htm; KBH reaction: https://parameter.io/kb-home-kbh-stock-drops-despite-q3-earnings-win-on-weak-margin-forecast/. These are two different companies' documents.

findings.finding: MHO's own Q2 10-Q shows rising pressure on Q3 margins. Incentives were $63.2M in Q2 against $47.1M a year earlier, with mortgage-rate buydowns up $22.0M. Homebuilding gross margin was 19.7% against 22.6%, and company gross margin 22.1%. There were 2,839 unsold homes under construction, more than the 2,426-unit backlog, plus $4.2M of inventory charges and $4.0M of Florida warranty charges. Management wrote that 'market conditions may persist through the remainder of 2026'. With rates about 30-50bp higher during Q3, clearing those specs costs more. Yet consensus of $3.25 implies EPS up from Q2 adjusted $3.14.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025: gross margin was 23.9% of revenue with $7.6M of inventory charges; the stock fell 6.14%. Q2 2026: margin 22.1% (down 260bp) on a record-orders quarter; the stock rose 1.54%.
findings.why_not_priced: The spec count (2,839, carrying value $600.7M) sits in a 10-Q note, not in the press release or the wire copy. A consensus that had priced spec clearance at 7% rates would sit at or below Q2's $3.14, not at $3.25. On the call management said only that backlog margin is 'pretty consistent'.
findings.independence: The same lever shows at peers: KBH lowered its Q4 margin guide (https://parameter.io/kb-home-kbh-stock-drops-despite-q3-earnings-win-on-weak-margin-forecast/), and NAHB's incentive share hit 66% in September (https://eyeonhousing.org/2026/09/builder-sentiment-falls-on-higher-interest-rates-and-costs/).

findings.finding: The Q3 order comparison is easy and community count is growing. Q3 2025 new contracts were 1,908 (-6%) on 234 average communities, about 2.7 per community per month. Q2 2026 set a record 2,387 (+15%) at 3.4 per month with cancellations at 8%. Management expects 2026 average community count about +5% with more openings in the second half. Even with a seasonal pace drop to about 2.8 per month on about 240 communities, Q3 orders would print about 2,000, up about 5% year on year, against peers at -9% to -12%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders are the line MHO trades on. Q3 2025 orders -6%: stock -6.14%. Q2 2026 orders +15% record: stock +1.54% (damped). Q1 2026: +3.69%.
findings.why_not_priced: The peer prints (-9%, -12%) and the October NAHB low set the sector's frame. A stock pricing a year-on-year order gain would not sit 4.6% above its 52-week low with downside skew. Partly priced, because buy-side models will know the comparison.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 pace and community guidance: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000799292/000079929226000025/exhibit991earningspressrel.htm and https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/MHO/Q22026. Census August new home sales hit a 2026 high at 684k (https://gvwire.com/2026/09/24/us-new-home-sales-jump-to-eight-month-high-in-august/).

findings.finding: On 2026-08-12 the board approved a new $250M repurchase authorization, replacing the prior one, which had $120.3M left at June 30; the stock rose 5.1% on the news. The run-rate had been $50M a quarter. With the stock now at $123, about 0.96x June 30 book of $127.88, Q3 and Q4 repurchases are accretive to book and a call statement on pace can support the shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The announcement itself moved the stock +5.1% (Aug 12-13). Buybacks ($50M a quarter) have accompanied mixed print reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public. What is not known is the Q3 dollar amount: buying after a 20% fall would show up as a larger-than-$50M figure and fewer diluted shares. A market expecting heavy below-book buying would not hold the stock under book.
findings.independence: The stock move is from https://www.webull.com/news/15398640174572544. Book value and the remaining authorization are from the Q2 release and 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000799292/000079929226000028/mho-20260630.htm).

findings.finding: Revenue bar risk from backlog conversion. Consensus revenue of $1.11B implies about 2,340 deliveries at about $460K plus about $33M of financial services, which is about 96% of the 2,426-unit June backlog. Conversion was 89% in Q3 2025 (2,296 of 2,577), 98% in Q2 2026 and about 106% in Q1 2026. A Q3-2025-like conversion gives about 2,160 deliveries and about $1.03B of revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: deliveries -6% and revenue -9%, yet the stock rose 1.54% on orders. Deliveries are secondary to orders for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: This is my own inference. The bar is disputed: Benzinga's $1.08B already sits below MarketBeat's $1.11B. Capped small for that reason.
findings.independence: None from a different source; it shares documents with the order finding.

findings.finding: Insiders sold near the top: CFO Phillip Creek sold 20,000 shares at $149.56 on 2026-08-04, cutting his holding 39%. Form 144s were filed 07-09, 07-31 and 08-03 to 08-05, with Form 4s on 08-04, 08-06 and 08-13. No insider buying was found after the fall.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No observable reaction to insider filings for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: These filings are public and old, and are largely priced. If insiders thought the stock cheap at $123, buying Form 4s would have appeared; none had by the EDGAR listing read on 2026-10-20.

baseline_tension: The negatives (rates, NAHB, peer margin guides, spec inventory) agree with the downside skew and the -13.7% run-up, so they are largely priced and kept moderate. The positives (easy order comparison, buyback at below book) cut against the skew; the reason to keep them is that the stock already discounts a sector-level order slump that MHO's Q2 did not show.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 / pessimism artefact: the macro finding agrees with a downside skew and a -13.7% run-up, so it was cut from -1.0 to -0.7 as mostly priced.
Lesson 6: the revenue bar is disputed ($1.11B vs $1.08B), so the backlog-conversion finding was capped from -0.3 to -0.2.
Lesson 5: the insider sale is old public information and a weak proxy; cut from -0.2 to -0.1.

The peer-print finding (a peer reporting after the company last spoke) was left at -0.8, as the 'what has worked' section supports it; the 10-Q spec and incentive finding was left at -0.8 as a primary-document number.
